speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; can you tell me how long you have had this rash and if you have noticed any changes in its appearance or symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the rash has persisted for five months, is itchy, and fluctuates in severity. Since you denied recent illnesses or new exposures, are you experiencing joint pain, fever, or oral ulcers? REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, ANA.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Dermatomyositis. Given the chronic pruritic rash on the upper extremities and the absence of systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain, along with normal initial labs, the most likely diagnosis is dermatomyositis. I recommend requesting images of the rash to confirm the characteristic heliotrope or Gottron's papules.
